meta.title: HariBatti — Jaipur signal countdowns and signal audits
meta.description: Live signal countdowns for Jaipur drivers and a timing audit for traffic police, built on 24-hour counts from 8 Mansarovar junctions. Reads signals, never controls them.

hero.lede: HariBatti tells drivers when the light will change, and shows traffic police where red waits run long and greens run short. It reads signals. It never controls them.

wait.title: Hours Jaipur lost while you read this
wait.method: Estimate: 7.5 lakh cars × 121 rush-hour hours each per year (TomTom 2025) ÷ 3.15 crore seconds in a year ≈ 2.9 hours lost every second.
wait.survey: On Monday 11 May 2026, {total} vehicles crossed the 8 surveyed Mansarovar junctions in 24 hours.
wait.peak: Busiest evening hour: {pcu} passenger-car units through {name} alone.

squeeze.title: Greens too short to clear the queue
squeeze.p1: Many fixed signals split green time evenly. On the Mansarovar corridor the main road carries 66–90% of the evening peak, so side streets get green they cannot use while the main road waits.
squeeze.stat1Note: Survey counts with assumed lanes and timing — to be confirmed with stopwatch timings.
squeeze.stat2Label: of evening traffic turns right at J03–J08
squeeze.stat2Note: Right turns need protected time, or they starve.
squeeze.stat3Label: that riders wait when a green is starved
squeeze.ped: Wide roads also leave pedestrians too little time to cross.

map.title: Eight junctions, counted for 24 hours
map.lede: Professional turning-movement counts, every 15 minutes, by vehicle type — Monday 11 and Tuesday 12 May 2026. Pick a junction.
map.healthNote: 0–100 from red wait, cycles to clear, starved greens, pedestrian time and spillback. Survey counts + assumed timing.
map.noWebgl: The 3D map needs WebGL. The junction list below has the same data.

itms.title: Rambagh Circle showed AI signals work
itms.p1: Jaipur Police's AI-ITMS trial at Rambagh Circle saved 8–45 seconds per lane. The system is now rolling out to 253 of the city's 423 signalised junctions.
itms.p2: HariBatti builds on that work. It adds what drivers and auditors cannot see yet: the countdown on your phone, and a fairness check on every phase.
itms.credit: Credit: Jaipur Police and Data Core Infotech. HariBatti is independent and not affiliated.

solution.title: One read-only data layer, three tools
solution.appText: Countdowns for the next three signals on your route, spoken in Hindi or English. Advice is only ever “hold 30 km/h” or “prepare to stop” — never “go”, never above the limit minus 5 km/h.
solution.commandText: A dashboard for the Traffic DCP and the Abhay Command Centre: junction health, a fairness audit, what-if timing plans and a local AI copilot.
solution.reportsText: A monthly report on waits, stops and pedestrian time, in English and Hindi, ready for the press.

wave.title: Ride J03 to J08 with fewer stops
wave.lede: A scooter rides the six signals in a row. Without advice it rides at 40 km/h and brakes at every red. With HariBatti it follows GLOSA v2: the fastest speed, up to the limit minus 5 km/h, that still reaches the next green.
wave.note: Simulated on the assumed signal plans, 500 m spacing. Speed advice never exceeds the limit minus 5 km/h.
wave.tradeoff: In this model GLOSA v2 removes more than half the stops and also shortens the ride. Fuel stays about the same, because the advised speed is higher than the 40 km/h cruise.

ai.title: Machine learning that stays checkable
ai.predictText: Seconds to the next change, with a confidence band. Exact only with the police feed.
ai.visionText: Vehicle counts and queue length from existing cameras, later.
ai.auditText: Every phase ranked by starved green and pedestrian time.
ai.copilotText: Officers ask in Hindi or English. It answers with the data and the SQL it used. Runs locally — no paid AI service.
ai.eventsText: Saved plans for SMS Stadium matches, Teej and Gangaur processions.

impact.title: What a few seconds per vehicle add up to
impact.assumptions: Assumptions you can change: idle burn 0.6 L/h (car), petrol ₹{price}/L, 2.31 kg CO₂ per litre. Default vehicles per junction come from the survey average.

pilot.title: A 60-day free pilot on the Mansarovar corridor
pilot.p1: Read-only access to phase and countdown data for the 8 pilot junctions. No control rights. Data stays in India, police own all data and reports, and the pilot can be switched off at any time.
pilot.subject: HariBatti pilot — Mansarovar corridor
pilot.team: Built by Krishna Mathur (B.Tech CSE AI/ML, MAIB at SP Jain).

footer.affiliation: Independent project, not affiliated with Rajasthan Police or Jaipur Traffic Police.
footer.privacy: Privacy: this site sets no tracking cookies. The app will ask before using location, keep it only during a ride and never tie it to a person.
footer.data: Survey figures are aggregates of the May 2026 counts. Every simulated number is labelled.

mix.title: Who is on the road
mix.lede: Every vehicle counted at the 8 junctions on 11–12 May 2026, by class. The survey converts them to passenger-car units (PCU), so a two-wheeler counts as half a car and a bus as three. Pick a class to see its 3D model.
mix.noModel: No 3D model for this class yet
mix.fit: PCU factors are the survey's own: they reproduce every one of its PCU totals exactly (R² = {r2}).
mix.autos: The survey counts autos together with cars.
